rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: People used to arrive early for the Prophet’s food and linger after eating; this occasioned the instruction on entering his home.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان ناس يتحينون طعامه، عليه الصلاة والسلام،

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar asked that the Prophet’s wives be veiled because righteous and wicked visitors alike entered upon them; the veil verse followed.
rows.anchor: فعمر قال: يا رسول الله، إن نساءك يدخل عليهن البار والفاجر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports that a companion’s hand touched Aisha’s during a meal, which displeased the Prophet and occasioned the veil verse.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: طعم معه بعض أصحابه، ومعهم عائشة، فمست يد رجل منهم يد عائشة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the occasion concerned a particular event, entry into any of the Prophet’s houses requires permission, whether for a meal or another purpose.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز دخول بيوته، عليه السلام، إلا بإذن، سواء كان لطعام أم لغيره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “houses” generalizes the rule to all the Prophet’s homes although the incident occurred in one particular house.
rows.anchor: وبيوت: جمع، وإن كانت الواقعة في بيت واحد خاص يعم جميع بيوته.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari construes the permission clause as a time expression and makes the exception govern both time and the state of waiting.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: إلا أن يؤذن في معنى الظرف تقديره: وقت أن يؤذن لكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Zamakhshari’s time-expression analysis: classical grammarians do not treat the مصدرية أن clause as a temporal adverbial.
rows.anchor: فليس بصحيح، وقد نصوا على أن أن المصدرية لا تكون في معنى الظرف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the majority disallow an exception governing time and state together, though al-Akhfash and al-Kisa’i allow this construction with a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الأخفش والكسائي ذلك في الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission clause can instead mean “except by permission,” with the preposition expressing cause or accompaniment.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يؤذن لكم، فلا يتعين أن يكون ظرفا، لأنه يكون التقدير: إلا بأن يؤذن لكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Not waiting” is a circumstantial phrase whose omitted governing verb is approximately “enter by permission, not waiting.”
rows.anchor: ومعنى غير ناظرين فحال، والعامل فيه محذوف تقديره: ادخلوا بالإذن غير ناظرين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means not waiting for the food to become ready or reach its proper time.
rows.anchor: أي غير منتظرين وقته، أي وقت استوائه وتهيئته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers vocalize “غير” in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase; Ibn Abi Ablah reads it in the genitive as an adjective for food.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: غير بالنصب على الحال وابن أبي عبلة: بالكسر، صفة لطعام.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari objects that the genitive reading leaves the understood pronoun referring to a different possessor unexpressed.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وليس بالوجه، لأنه جرى على غير من هو له،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that Kufan grammarians permit omission of that pronoun when no ambiguity results.
rows.anchor: وحذف هذا الضمير جائز عند الكوفيين إذا لم يلبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “إناه” means the food’s readiness or, according to another explanation, its appointed mealtime.
rows.anchor: وأنى الطعام إدراكه، يقال: أنى الطعام أنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers have إناه without a long vowel after the nun; al-A‘mash reads إناءه with a long vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: إناه مفردا والأعمش: إناءه، بمدة بعد النون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order is to enter only after being invited, then to leave after eating; “and not lingering for conversation” is coordinated with the waiting prohibition.
rows.anchor: ورتب تعالى الدخول على أن يدعوا، فلا يقدمون عليه الدخول حين يدعوا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordination permits either a genitive or accusative parsing of “not lingering”; a further analysis supplies an omitted circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: ولا مستأنسين لحديث: معطوف على ناظرين، فهو مجرور أو معطوف على غير،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may express the purpose of prolonging conversation or strengthen the active participle’s object, meaning the household’s conversation.
rows.anchor: واللام في لحديث إما لام العلة، نهوا أن يطيلوا الجلوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istī’nās here is listening to conversation and relieving one another’s loneliness.
rows.anchor: واستئناسه: تسمعه وتوحشه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting and lingering distress the Prophet because he was shy to make visitors leave; God does not refrain from stating what is right.
rows.anchor: إن ذلكم: أي انتظاركم واستئناسكم، يؤذي النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Telling visitors to leave is right; “God is not shy of the truth” means He does not refrain from it, by contrast with the Prophet’s embarrassment.
rows.anchor: يعني أن إخراجكم حق ما ينبغي أن يستحيا منه.

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha’s reported remark is that God’s refusal to tolerate boors is enough to identify them as boors.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة، وابن عباس: حسبك في الثقلاء، أن الله لم يحتملهم.

rows.speaker: إسماعيل بن أبي حكيم
rows.claim: After hearing the verse recited, Isma‘il ibn Abi Hakim called it divine etiquette for boors.
rows.anchor: هنا أدب أدب الله به الثقلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group reads فيستحيي with a kasra on the ḥāʾ, using the Tamimi form of the verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة: فيستحيي بكسر الحاء، مضارع استحا، وهي لغة بني تميم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians dispute whether the weak verb’s deleted letter is its middle radical or final radical, which changes its morphological pattern.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا ما المحذوف، أعين الكلمة أم لامها؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Household goods includes the ordinary utensils and amenities sought in shared domestic life for religious and worldly needs.
rows.anchor: والمتاع عام في ما يمكن أن يطلب على عرف السكنى والمجاورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The veil is purer because sight can prompt desire and temptation between men and women.
rows.anchor: أطهر: يريد من الخواطر التي تخطر للرجال في أمر النساء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited couplet says a person who keeps moving the eye remains exposed to danger, since pleasure of sight may harm the heart.
rows.anchor: والمرء ما دام ذاعين يقلبها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وبعض الصحابة
rows.claim: Some people allegedly said they might marry a named woman after Muhammad’s death; Ibn Abbas and some companions identify her as Aisha.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وبعض الصحابة: وفلانة عائشة.

rows.speaker: معمر
rows.claim: Makkī transmits from Ma‘mar that the man who made the remark was Talha ibn Ubayd Allah.
rows.anchor: وحكى مكي عن معمر أنه قال: هو طلحة بن عبيد الله.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the attribution to Talha is unsound because God protected him from such conduct.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا عندي لا يصح على طلحة فإن الله عصمه منه.

rows.speaker: التحرير
rows.claim: Al-Taḥrīr names Talha and says he repented, freed a slave, gave ten camels in God’s cause, and performed pilgrimage on foot.
rows.anchor: وفي التحرير أنه طلحة، فنزلت: ولا أن تنكحوا أزواجه من بعده أبدا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report attributes to a hypocrite the threat that men would draw lots for the Prophet’s wives after his death.
rows.anchor: وروي أن بعض المنافقين قال: حين تزوج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Qutayla’s tribe returned from apostasy, Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl married her; the Prophet had married her but had not consummated the marriage.
rows.anchor: تزوج عكرمة ابن أبي جهل قتيلة بنت الأشعث بن قيس

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar reassured Abu Bakr that Qutayla was not one of the Prophet’s wives because the marriage was unconsummated and no veil had been imposed.
rows.anchor: إنها ليست من نسائه، إنه لم يبن بها، ولا أرخى عليها حجابا،

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت عميس
rows.claim: Asma bint Umays showed Umar an Ethiopian method for veiling a woman’s coffin in a domed litter; Umar refused it, though a report says it was used at Fatima’s funeral.
rows.anchor: فدلته أسماء بنت عميس على سترها في النعش في القبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general prohibition on harming the Messenger is followed by a specific prohibition on marrying his wives, an especially grave form of harm.
rows.anchor: وما كان لكم أن تؤذوا رسول الله: عام في كل ما يتأذى به، ولا أن تنكحوا: خاص بعد عام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition magnifies God’s regard for the Prophet and establishes his sanctity in life and after death.
rows.anchor: وهذا من إعلام تعظيم الله لرسوله، وإيجابه حرمته حيا وميتا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule consoles the Prophet, since a jealous husband may fear his wife marrying another after his death, especially among Arabs.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من تفرط غيرته على حرمته حتى يتمنى لها الموت،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari tells of a young man who kissed his beloved while imagining her surviving him and belonging to another.
rows.anchor: وحكى الزمخشري أن بعض الفتيان قبل جارية كان يحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Zamakhshari’s use of “ما عسى” as a relative clause, saying this construction is not permitted.
rows.anchor: فجعل عسى صلة للموصول، وقد كثر منه هذا وهو لا يجوز.

rows.speaker: بعض الفقهاء
rows.claim: Some jurists liken a second husband’s share in “the roaring third” to a form of punishment; the author says the Prophet’s deed observed this.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض الفقهاء، أن الزوج الثاني في هدير الثلث يجري مجرى العقوبة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about what people reveal or conceal covers both spoken and inward intentions concerning the Prophet’s wives or any other hurtful act.
rows.anchor: إن تبدوا شيئا على ألسنتكم، أو تخفوه في صدوركم، مما يقع عليه العقاب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says relatives asked whether they too must speak to the Prophet’s wives from behind a veil, and the next verse exempted them.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه لما نزلت آية الحجاب قال: الآباء والأبناء والأقارب،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains “no blame” as permission for the women to leave the veil in the specified context.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: في ترك الحجاب.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the permission as setting aside the outer garment and displaying adornment.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: في وضع الجلباب وإبداء الزينة.

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha‘bi says uncles and maternal uncles are omitted because they might describe a woman to their sons, who are not her unmarriageable kin.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: لم يذكر العم والخال، وإن كانا من المحارم، لئلا يصفا للأبناء،

rows.speaker: الشعبي وعكرمة
rows.claim: Al-Sha‘bi and Ikrima disliked women removing the head covering before an uncle or maternal uncle; another explanation treats them like parents.
rows.anchor: وقد كره الشعبي وعكرمة أن تضع المرأة خمارها عند عمها أو خالها،

rows.speaker: ابن زيد وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and others take “their women” to mean all believing women, with the possessive marking faith.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وغيره: أراد جميع النساء المؤمنات، وتخصيص الإضافة إنما هي في الأيمان.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid likewise interprets “their women” as women of their own religion.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: من أهل دينهن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordinary sense of “those whom their right hands possess” includes both male and female slaves; other interpreters restrict or broaden it differently.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من قوله: أو ما ملكت أيمانهن، دخول العبيد والإماء دون ما ملك غيرهن.

rows.speaker: النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Nakha‘i permits a woman’s slave to see the body ordinarily covered by her dress.
rows.anchor: وقال النخعي: يباح لعبدها النظر إلى ما يواريه الدرع من ظاهر بدنها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet ordered a veil from Umm Salama’s scribe-slave Nabhan when he could afford his contract, and she complied.
rows.anchor: فقد أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بضرب الحجاب دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God shifts from speaking about the women to addressing them directly and includes observing the limits of the veil instruction.
rows.anchor: واتقين الله: أمر بالتقوى وخروج من الغيبة إلى الخطاب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers put “His angels” in the accusative; Ibn Abbas and a transmission from Abu Amr read it nominative, with competing grammatical explanations.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وملائكته نصبا وابن عباس، وعبد الوارث عن أبي عمرو: رفعا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading is parsed by Kufans (except al-Farra’) as coordinated with the position of “inna’s” noun, while Basrans supply an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: فعند الكوفيين غير الفراء هو عطف على موضع اسم إن، والفراء يشترط خفاء إعراب اسم إن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes differ over whether prayer upon the Prophet is obligatory or recommended; if obligatory, one view requires it once in every gathering when he is mentioned.
rows.anchor: والظاهر وجوب الصلاة والسلام عليه، وقيل: سنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says companions knew how to greet the Prophet but asked how to pray for him; he taught a formula invoking blessing on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham and his family.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية قال قوم من الصحابة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the threat against those who hurt God and His Messenger was revealed about people who criticized the Prophet’s marriage to Safiyya bint Huyayy.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في الذين طعنوا عليه حين اتخذ صفية بنت حيي زوجا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A separate account relates the verse to criticism of the Prophet’s appointment of Usama ibn Zayd.
rows.anchor: والطعن في تأمير أسامة بن زيد: أن إيذاءه عليه السلام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harming God and the Messenger includes disbelief, sins, denying prophethood, violating revelation, and every kind of injury to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: فعل ما نهى الله ورسوله عنه من الكفر والمعاصي، وإنكار النبوة ومخالفة الشرع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because literal harm cannot apply to God, interpreters say the phrase means harming God’s allies or His Messenger, or remove an implied word.
rows.anchor: ولا يتصور الأذى حقيقة في حق الله، فقيل: هو على حذف مضاف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations identify claims by Jews, Christians, and polytheists, including that God has a son, partners, or daughters.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في أذى الله، هو قول اليهود والنصارى والمشركين: يد الله مغلولة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima applies harming God to image-makers who imitate God’s creation.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة: فعل أصحاب التصاوير الذين يزورون خلقا مثل خلق الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harming the Messenger is also explained as calling him a sorcerer, poet, soothsayer, or madman, or injuring him at Uhud.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في أذى رسول الله قولهم: ساحر شاعر كاهن مجنون،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “without having earned it” distinguishes wrongful injury to believers from injury that may be deserved.
rows.anchor: ومعنى بغير ما اكتسبوا: بغير جناية واستحقاق أذى.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says this was revealed about hypocrites who tormented and abused Ali.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: نزلت في ناس من المنافقين يؤذون عليا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says men in Medina sat in public places to watch, accost, and proposition women; the garment instruction followed.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه كان في المدينة قوم يجلسون على الصعدات لرؤية النساء ومعارضتهن ومراودتهن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported meanings of jilbab include an outer wrap, head covering, mantle, any garment worn over clothes, or anything used for concealment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الجلباب: كل ثوب تلبسه المرأة فوق ثيابها،

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd’s poetic phrase “I wrapped myself in the blackness of night” uses jilbab for a covering.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد: تجلببت من سواد الليل جلبابا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima describes drawing one side of the jilbab across the other so the woman is not seen.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: تلقي جانب الجلباب على غيرها ولا يرى.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة السلماني
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda al-Salmani describes placing the wrap above the brow and bringing it over the nose.
rows.anchor: أن تضع رداءها فوق الحاجب، ثم تديره حتى تضعه على أنفها.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the woman covers one eye, her forehead, and the other side while leaving an eye visible; the author notes this Andalusian custom.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: تغطي إحدى عينيها وجبهتها والشق الآخر إلا العين.

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa’i understands the women to draw their mantles close around themselves.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: يتقنعن بملاحفهن منضمة عليهن،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada describe wrapping the garment over the forehead and nose; the eyes may remain visible while the chest and most of the face are covered.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، وقتادة: وذلك أن تلويه فوق الجبين وتشده، ثم تعطفه على الأنف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “believing women” appears general enough to include enslaved women as well as free women; excluding them requires clear evidence.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: ونساء المؤمنين يشمل الحرائر والإماء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition “من” is partitive, and “upon them” may cover the whole body or specifically the face, which was exposed before Islam.
rows.anchor: ومن في: من جلابيبهن للتبعيض، وعليهن: شامل لجميع أجسادهن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covering lets women be recognized as chaste and protects them from harassment; the ending reassures them about conduct before the command.
rows.anchor: ذلك أدنى أن يعرفن: لتسترهن بالعفة، فلا يتعرض لهن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following threat concerns three types of people who harm the community: hypocrites, those with lustful illness, and rumor-spreaders; the labels may mark three groups or three traits in one group.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المؤذون ثلاثة، باعتبار إذايتهم لله ولرسوله وللمؤمنين،

rows.speaker: عكرمة والسدي
rows.claim: Ikrima explains “those in whose hearts is disease” as sexual desire and lust; al-Suddi explains it as hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: الذين في قلوبهم مرض، هو العزل وحب الزنا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several readings vary the form of “their faces turning”; the author prefers the first reading’s sense of movement or transformation of faces in every direction.
rows.anchor: وقراءة ابن أبي عبلة: تتقلب بتاءين، وتقليب الوجوه في النار: تحركها في الجهات،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The face can stand for the whole person, and it is the human’s most honored part; if it is overturned in fire, the rest is all the more so.
rows.anchor: والوجه أشرف ما في الإنسان، فإذا قلب في النار كان تقليب ما سواه أولى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned people’s wish and their complaints about their leaders occur too late to help them.
rows.anchor: وتمنيهم حيث لا ينفع، وتشكيهم من كبرائهم لا يجدي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use سادتنا; it is an unusual plural pattern unless treated as the plural of سائد.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: سادتنا، جمعا على وزن فعلات، أصله سودة،

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء وقتادة والسلمي وابن عامر
rows.claim: These authorities and the common Basran reading use ساداتنا, a plural with alif and tāʾ that is not generally productive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن، وأبو رجاء، وقتادة، والسلمي، وابن عامر، والعامة

rows.speaker: قتادة وطاوس وأبو أسامة
rows.claim: They explain the “leaders” as chiefs, notables, and commanders who taught and embellished disbelief.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: سادتنا: رؤساؤنا. وقال طاوس: أشرافنا وقال أبو أسامة: أمراؤنا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poetic line uses sādah for leaders, followed by the lexical note that ḍalla can take “the way” directly or with عن.
rows.anchor: ويقال: ضل السبيل، وضل عن السبيل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for their leaders to receive double punishment: one for their own error and one for misleading others.
rows.anchor: ربنا آتهم ضعفين من العذاب: ضعفا على ضلالهم في أنفسهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers say كثيرا; Hudhayfa, Ibn Amir, Asim, and al-A‘raj (in one transmission) read كبيرا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: كثيرا بالثاء المثلثة. وقرأ حذيفة بن اليمان، وابن عامر، وعاصم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with Moses is linked either to the Zayd–Zaynab episode and gossip or to the slander against Aisha.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت في شأن زيد وزينب، وما سمع فيه من قالة بعض الناس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet invoked mercy on Moses after an accuser challenged his distribution, saying Moses had endured worse and remained patient.
rows.anchor: رحم الله أخي موسى، لقد أوذي أكثر من هذا فصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was accused of bodily defects and of envying and killing his brother Aaron.
rows.anchor: وإذاية موسى قولهم: إنه أبرص وآدر، وأنه حسد أخاه هارون وقتله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust most likely encompasses every charge entrusted to people, including commands and prohibitions and religious and worldly duties; the whole revealed law is a trust.
rows.anchor: والأمانة: الظاهر أنها كل ما يؤتمن عليه من أمر ونهي وشأن دين ودنيا.

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka‘b gives the example of a woman being entrusted with guarding her sexual chastity.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال أبي زين كعب: من الأمانة أن اؤتمنت المرأة على فرجها.

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda considers washing after major ritual impurity a trust.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء: غسل الجنابة أمانة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offer to the immense created bodies and their refusal and fear can be literal, since God may grant created things perception, as in other miracles.
rows.anchor: وهذا غير مستحيل، إذ قد سبح الحصى في كفه عليه الصلاة والسلام، وحن الجذع إليه،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says inanimate things were given understanding and discrimination and offered a choice about carrying the trust; mountains are singled out to emphasize the burden.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أعطيت الجمادات فهما وتمييزا، فخيرت في الحمل،

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the offer was audible to Adam and the refusal audible from inanimate things, demonstrating the trust and Adam’s zeal and distinction.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: عرضت بمسمع من آدم، عليه الصلاة والسلام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations treat the passage figuratively, either by ellipsis for the beings in the heavens and earth or as personification.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو مجاز، فقيل: من مجاز الحذف، أي على من فيها من الملائكة،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari reads the scene as an imagined comparison that dramatizes how weighty human obligations would be even for the mightiest created bodies.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أن ما كلفه الإنسان بلغ من عظمه وثقل محمله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari compares the figurative speech to Arabic sayings that make fat or animals speak, though the imagined speech is impossible in fact.
rows.anchor: من ذلك قول العرب: لو قيل للشحم أين تذهب لقيل: أسوي العوج

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari answers that the comparison is mentally posited as a hypothetical, so an impossible imagined scene can illustrate the real weight of obligation.
rows.anchor: الممثل به في الآية، وفي قولهم: لو قيل للشحم أين تذهب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He also argues that inanimate bodies submit to God in ways appropriate to them, while humans are capable of obeying commands and prohibitions but fail to do so.
rows.anchor: هذه الأجرام العظام قد انقادت لأمر الله انقياد مثلها،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: On this allegorical reading, the trust means obedience; the heavens and earth decline it figuratively, while humans accept it and fail to discharge it.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأمانة: الطاعة، لأنها لازمة للوجود. كما أن الأمانة لازمة للأداء،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: “Carrying” an obligation is a metaphor based on the trust riding on its custodian until performance clears the debt.
rows.anchor: وحمل الأمانة من قولك: فلان حامل للأمانة ومحتمل لها،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The human is called unjust for failing to discharge the trust and ignorant for missing the benefit of fulfilling it despite being able.
rows.anchor: ثم وصفه بالظلم لكونه تاركا لأداء الأمانة، وبالجهل لخطئه ما يسعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zamakhshari’s allegorical explanation contains an omitted element, as the author notes.
rows.anchor: انتهى، وفيه بعض حذف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another figurative reading compares the trust’s weight with the strength of the heavens, earth, and mountains: they would fall short and refuse if they could speak.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: الآية من المجاز، أي إذا قايسنا ثقل الأمانة بقوة السموات والأرض والجبال،

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr explains “عرضنا” as comparing the trust with the created bodies, and “أبين” as being unable to bear it.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قول ابن بحر» معنى عرضنا: عارضناها وقابلناها بها.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jubayr say the human accepted responsibility for the trust’s duties; the human is Adam, unjust to himself and ignorant of the burden.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وابن جبير: التزم القيام بحقها، والإنسان آدم،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Adam did not last even a day before being expelled from Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ما تم له يوم حتى أخرج من الجنة.

rows.speaker: الضحاك والحسن
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Hasan interpret carrying the trust as betraying it; the human refers to unbelievers, hypocrites, and sinners in differing degrees.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك، والحسن: وحملها معناه: خان فيها،

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud and another report from Ibn Abbas identify the human with Cain, who had promised Adam to protect the family while Adam was away.
rows.anchor: وكان قد تحمل لأبيه أمانة أن يحفظ الأهل بعده،

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq interprets the trust as signs of divine oneness in created things and carrying it as betrayal or taking it away.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: عرض الأمانة: وضع شواهد الوحدانية في المصنوعات:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Ibn Ishaq’s cited poem does not prove that “carrying” means taking something away; it can mean continually assuming further trusts.
rows.anchor: وليس وتحمل أخرى نصا في الذهاب بها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “so that He may punish” marks an eventual outcome: the trust was not accepted in order to be punished, but its acceptance led to punishment for hypocrites and idolaters.
rows.anchor: واللام في ليعذب لام الصيرورة، لأنه لم يحملها لأن يعذب،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari calls the lām causal figuratively because punishment is the consequence of carrying the trust, as discipline results from striking.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لام التعليل على طريق المجاز، لأن نتيجة حمل الأمانة العذاب،

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A‘mash reads فيتوب in the indicative, making the clause begin a separate statement rather than continue the preceding purpose.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: فيتوب، يعني بالرفع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordinary reading means God punishes those who betray the trust and turns in mercy to believers who did not betray it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قراءة العامة: ليعذب الله حامل الأمانة ويتوب على غيره ممن لم يحملها،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan also reads ويتوب with the indicative ending.
rows.anchor: وذهب صاحب اللوامح أن الحسن قرأ ويتوب بالرفع.

none: Qur’an verse text only; no commentary claim appears in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This Meccan surah continues the warning and rebuke at the end of Surat al-Mu’min by announcing a clear revelation and confronting Quraysh’s rejection.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مكية بلا خلاف، ومناسبتها لما قبلها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its warning anticipates the fate of Quraysh’s leaders through killing, capture, plunder, and enslavement, like the destruction of ‘Ad and Thamud.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قريش حل بصناديدها من القتل والأسر والنهب والسبي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report recounts that after the Prophet recited the warning of a thunderbolt like that of ‘Ad and Thamud, Utba trembled, stopped him, and admitted the recitation was neither poetry, sorcery, nor soothsaying.
rows.anchor: فلما تكلم عتبة، قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: حم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s progression moves from the rejection of revelation to God’s power to create the upper and lower worlds, then warns the rejecters.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر قدرة الإله على إيجاد العالم العلوي والسفلي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tanzīl” is parsed as a predicate with an omitted subject, a subject whose predicate is “a book,” or a predicate of Ḥā Mīm; “book” may be an apposition.
rows.anchor: تنزيل، رفع على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف، أي هذا تنزيل عند الفراء،

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains “its verses are made distinct” as clarified and explained, distinguishing lawful and forbidden, commands and prohibitions, and promise and threat.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: بينت آياته، أي فسرت معانيه،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the verses are differentiated by promise and threat.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: بالوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan explains the distinction as reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان: بالثواب والعقاب.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verses distinguish Muhammad from those who oppose him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: بين محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ومن خالفه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation points to the varied pauses and verse endings, which follow neither poetic rhyme nor ordinary sajʿ.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فصلت بالمواقف وأنواع، أواخر الآي، ولم يكن يرجع إلى قافية

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi catalogs the Qur’an’s subject matter: divine attributes, creation, duties, rewards, punishments, exhortation, moral training, and histories.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: ميزت آياته، وجعل تفاصيل معان مختلفة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with fatḥa and a light ṣād means separating truth from falsehood or separating verses by their varied meanings.
rows.anchor: بفتح الفاء والصاد مخففة، أي فرقت بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Qur’ānan” has several parses: emphatic or preparatory circumstantial accusative, cognate accusative, honorific specification, or object of فصلت; grammarians differ on its referent.
rows.anchor: وانتصب قرآنا على أنه حال بنفسه، وهي مؤكدة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For a people who know” is attached to the differentiation: they understand the signs and benefit from them, so they are singled out in honor.
rows.anchor: ولقوم متعلق بفصلت، أي يعلمون الأشياء، ويعقلون الدلائل،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari allows the phrase to describe Arabic as language understood by its people, rebutting claims that the Qur’an contains non-Arabic words.
rows.anchor: وكأنه رد على من زعم أن في القرآن ما ليس من كلام العرب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good news and warning are explained as Paradise for believers and Fire for unbelievers; Zayd ibn Ali’s nominative reading may modify the book or serve as a predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: بشير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage continues the nominative reading, parsing “warner” as an adjective of the book or a predicate; it brings Paradise to believers and warns unbelievers of Hell.
rows.anchor: ونذير برفعهما على الصفة لكتاب، أو على خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an brings Paradise as good news to believers and warns unbelievers of the Fire.
rows.anchor: وبشارته بالجنة لمن آمن، ونذارته بالنار لمن كفر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most of the people turned away despite having knowledge because they failed to reflect fully; their lack of hearing is figurative for refusing and not benefiting.
rows.anchor: أي كانوا من أهل العلم ولكن لم ينظروا النظر التام، بل أعرضوا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts being covered and ears burdened are images of refusing revelation, like the earlier expression “our hearts are wrapped.”
rows.anchor: وهذه تمثيلات لامتناع قبول الحق، كأن قلوبهم في غلاف،

rows.speaker: طلحة
rows.claim: Talha reads وقر with a kasra on the wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة: وقر بكسر الواو،

rows.speaker: الفراء وغيره
rows.claim: The barrier between Muhammad and his audience signifies opposition in religion, since he worships God while they worship idols.
rows.anchor: والحجاب: الستر المانع من الإجابة، وهو خلاف في الدين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abu Jahl mocked the Prophet by covering his head with a cloth and claiming that a barrier stood between them.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن أبا جهل استغشى على رأسه ثوبا وقال: يا محمد، بيننا وبينك حجاب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations take the barrier as a figure for nonresponse or as an expression of enmity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تمثيل بعدم الإجابة. وقيل: عبارة عن العداوة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min marks the beginning of the barrier from both sides, filling the space between the Prophet and his opponents to intensify their separation.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أن الحجاب ابتدأ منا وابتدأ منك،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says “our hearts are in coverings” and “a covering is on our hearts” express the same meaning, but “in” more strongly suggests total enclosure and exclusion.
rows.anchor: إن في أبلغ في هذا الموضع من على،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The container image conveys complete inaccessibility, as with money inside a purse, unlike merely having a cover on the money.
rows.anchor: فلا يمكن أن يصل إليها شيء. كما تقول: المال في الكيس،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari notes that God’s statement about placing coverings on hearts does not need the rhetorical exaggeration used in the opponents’ boast.
rows.anchor: وأما في قوله: إنا جعلنا، فهو من إخبار الله تعالى، لا يحتاج إلى مبالغة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zamakhshari’s term “the fluent speakers” means Arab speakers and poets; ornate poetic artifice was criticized when overly deliberate.
rows.anchor: وقول الزمخشري: وترى المطابيع، يعني من العرب وشعرائهم،

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets “act; we are acting” as a threat: they will work toward the Prophet’s destruction.
rows.anchor: فاعمل إننا عاملون، قال الكلبي: في هلاكنا إنا عاملون في هلاكك.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says each side is invited to act for its own deity.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: اعمل لإلهك الذي أرسلك، فإننا عاملون لآلهتنا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra’ reads it as each side following its own religion.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: اعمل على مقتضى دينك، ونحن نعمل على مقتضى ديننا،

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi contrasts working for the afterlife with their work for worldly life.
rows.anchor: وذكر الماوردي: اعمل لآخرتك، فإنا نعمل لدنيانا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words may be a neutral mutual leave-taking or an expression of contempt.
rows.anchor: واحتمل قولهم: فاعمل إننا عاملون، أي تكون متاركة محضة، وأن يكون استخفافا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers have “Say” as an imperative; Ibn Waththab and al-A‘mash read “He said” as a past verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: قل على الأمر، وابن وثاب والأعمش: قال فعلا ماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nakha‘i and al-A‘mash read يوحي with a kasra on the ḥāʾ; most readers have a fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ النخعي والأعمش: يوحي بكسر الحاء والجمهور: بفتحها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is a human like his audience, but revelation distinguishes him; his message is to worship one God and reject their idols.
rows.anchor: وأخبر أنه بشر مثلهم لا ملك، لكنه أوحي إليه دونهم.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet was taught humility through revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: علمه تعالى التواضع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Be upright toward Him” means direct one’s devotion to God alone through monotheism, the head of religion; seeking forgiveness is the head of practice.
rows.anchor: فاستقيموا إليه: أي له بالتوحيد الذي هو رأس الدين والعمل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase استقيموا إليه uses إلى because istiqāma is made to include turning toward God.
rows.anchor: وضمن استقيموا معنى التوجه، فلذلك تعدى بإلى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human happiness requires reverence for God and compassion toward creatures; polytheists fail both and also deny resurrection.
rows.anchor: بأن السعادة مربوطة بأمرين: التعظيم لله والشفقة على خلقه

rows.speaker: ابن السائب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sa’ib takes zakat in its ordinary sense of almsgiving and says they performed pilgrimage but withheld alms.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الزكاة على ظاهرها من زكاة الأموال، قاله ابن السائب،

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: A reported interpretation says Quraysh fed pilgrims while depriving believers of food.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: وقيل: كانت قريش تطعم الحاج وتحرم من آمن منهم.

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Another interpretation from al-Hasan and Qatada says they did not believe in or acknowledge zakat.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة أيضا: المعنى لا يؤمنون بالزكاة، ولا يقرون بها.

rows.speaker: مجاهد والربيع
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Rabi‘ understand the phrase as failure to purify one’s deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والربيع: لا يزكون أعمالهم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والجمهور
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and most exegetes identify zakat here with the testimony of divine unity, supported by Moses’ call “will you purify yourself?”; the early Meccan setting predates obligatory monetary zakat.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والجمهور: الزكاة هنا لا إله إلا الله التوحيد،

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says this means purification of heart and body from idolatry and sins, a view also attributed to Mujahid and al-Rabi‘.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عطية، قال: وإنما هذه زكاة القلب والبدن

rows.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Muqatil interpret zakat as spending in obedience.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك ومقاتل: الزكاة هنا النفقة في الطاعة.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse was revealed concerning the sick and disabled who cannot complete acts of worship; they receive the reward for the deeds they would have done when healthy.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: نزلت في المرضى والزمنى إذا عجزوا عن إكمال الطاعات،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “without being diminished” as not reduced.
rows.anchor: والممنون: المنقوص، قاله ابن عباس،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the reward as not being counted or calculated.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: غير محسوب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the reward is never cut off, supported by a cited poem about generosity that is not withdrawn.
rows.anchor: وقيل: غير مقطوع، قال الشاعر: فضل الجواد على الخيل البطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says God does not reproach recipients for His gifts, since divine gifts confer honor whereas human gifts can invite reproach.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا يمن به لأن أعطيات الله تشريف،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says a gift should not be called a favor when it is owed; the author detects a Mu‘tazilite implication in this formulation.
rows.anchor: نقله الزمخشري، وفيه دسيسة الاعتزال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes people for disbelieving the creator of the lower and upper worlds, while explaining creation’s sequence and duration despite God’s ability to create instantly.
rows.anchor: استفهام توبيخ وتشنيع عليهم، يكفر من أوجد العالم سفليه وعلويه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Partners” are supposed equals among angels, jinn, and idols worshipped alongside God; al-Suddi also includes human leaders obeyed as equals.
rows.anchor: وتجعلون له أندادا: أي أشباها وأمثالا من الملائكة والجن والأصنام

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains the supposed equals as men whom people obey.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: أكفاء من الرجال يطيعونهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “And you make” is coordinated with “you disbelieve,” so both fall within the rebuking question; “that” refers to the creator of earth.
rows.anchor: وتجعلون معطوف على لتكفرون، فهو داخل في حيز الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He placed mountains in it” begins a fresh report and is coordinated with the earlier reproach, not embedded within its relative clause.
rows.anchor: وجعل فيها رواسي: إخبار مستأنف، وليس من الصلة في شيء،

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the earth’s provisions are the livelihoods and sustenance of its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وأضافهما إلى الأرض من حيث هي فيها وعنها برزت، قاله السدي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada includes the mountains, rivers, trees, rocks, minerals, and other things that sustain and benefit the earth.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: أقواتها من الجبال والأنهار والأشجار والصخور والمعادن،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the provisions as rain and water.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أقواتها من المطر والمياه.

rows.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد
rows.claim: They understand the provisions as regional specialties distributed across lands, making people dependent on one another for clothing, food, and crops.
rows.anchor: خصائصها التي قسمها في البلاد مما خص به كل إقليم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four days include the two already mentioned for creating the earth.
rows.anchor: في أربعة أيام: أي في تمام أربعة أيام باليومين المتقدمين.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari calls the four days the complete, exact duration for creating the earth and everything in it; al-Zajjaj instead calls them the remaining days after the first two.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري في أربعة أيام، فذلكة لمدة خلق

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi argues that “four days” makes clear the duration fully covers the creation work, unlike “two days.”
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: ويفقه من كلام الزمخشري في أربعة أيام فائدة زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Razi’s distinction: either duration may be understood as covering all days or only part of each counted day.
rows.anchor: ولا فرق بين يومين وأربعة أيام بالنسبة إلى الاستغراق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers vocalize سواء in the accusative; Abu Ja‘far reads it nominative, and several named readers use the genitive as an adjective of “days.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: سواء بالنصب على الحال وأبو جعفر بالرفع:

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi explain سواء as the same account for anyone asking about what happened and seeking a lesson.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة والسدي: معناه سواء لمن سأل عن الأمر واستفهم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد وجماعة
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and others take it to mean that creation’s provisions are fully prepared and available for needy people.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وجماعة: معناه مستو مهيأ أمر هذه المخلوقات

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari connects “for those who ask” either to people asking how long creation took or to those needing its provisions.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: بم تعلق قوله: للسائلين؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the earth, the passage turns to heaven; “He turned toward heaven” means He directed His will to creating it, without implying physical influence elsewhere.
rows.anchor: ثم استوى إلى السماء: أي قصد إليها وتوجه دون إرادة تأثير في غيرها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent account says heaven’s original material was smoke; a report from the Jewish Torah says heat over water raised foam and smoke, from which earth and heavens were made.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المادة التي خلقت منها السماء كانت دخانا.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya supplies omitted verbs for making, perfecting, and completing the heavens and earth before the command to come.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: هنا لفظ متروك يدل عليه الظاهر، وتقديره: فأوجدها وأتقنها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers literal speech after God grants heaven and earth life and perception; he acknowledges that others take their response figuratively.
rows.anchor: ورجح قول من ذهب إلى أنهما نطقتا نطقا حقيقيا،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari understands the command and their compliance as depicting their nonresistance to God’s creative will, not an actual exchange of speech.
rows.anchor: والغرض تصوير أثر قدرته في المقدورات لا غير، من غير أن يحقق شيء من الخطاب والجواب،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: To explain why earth is addressed although created earlier, Zamakhshari distinguishes creating its body from spreading it after the heaven, citing the earth’s later spreading.
rows.anchor: قد خلق جرم الأرض أولا غير مدحوة، ثم دحاها بعد خلق السماء،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes “come” mean assume the form and function God intends: earth as a settled dwelling and heaven as a roof.
rows.anchor: ائت يا أرض مدحوة قرارا ومهادا لأهلك، وائت يا سماء مقببة سقفا لهم.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He also allows the two to be commanded to meet each other in the complementary arrangement intended by wisdom.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: لتأت كل واحدة صاحبتها الإتيان الذي أريده

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari reads “willingly or unwillingly” as an image for the inescapable effect of divine power and parses both words as circumstantial accusatives.
rows.anchor: هو مثل للزوم تأثير قدرته فيهما، وأن امتناعهما من تأثير قدرته محال،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He explains the masculine plural طائعين by treating heaven and earth as speakers and responders, comparable to other masculine plurals used of them.
rows.anchor: لما جعلت مخاطبات ومجيبات، ووصفت بالطوع والكره، قيل: طائعين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد
rows.claim: They read أتيا and أتينا as forms from “to give,” meaning heaven and earth yielded their obedience.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد: أتيا على وزن فعلا،

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes this reading to mean that heaven and earth gave God the obedience He sought.
rows.anchor: وذلك بمعنى أعطيا من أنفسكما من الطاعة ما أردته منكما،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari instead derives the reading from mutual agreement: each was to comply with the other, and both agreed.
rows.anchor: أنه جعل هذه القراءة من المواتاة، وهي الموافقة،

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi also derives the long-vowel reading from agreement and says it means they hastened to comply; taking it as “give” would require an awkward omitted object.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون من الإيتاء الذي هو الإعطاء لبعد حذف مفعوله.

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A‘mash reads كرها with a ḍamma, a dialect variant; the author says the form more often means hardship.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: أو كرها بضم الكاف،

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya suggests “they said” refers to the plural groups of heavens and earth, expressed as singulars.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقوله قالتا، أراد الفرقتين المذكورتين:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Ibn Atiyya’s account: the text previously mentioned one heaven and one earth, so a natural dual is appropriate; the cited poem is a different construction.
rows.anchor: هذا وليس كما ذكر، لأنه إنما تقدم ذكر الأرض مفردة والسماء مفرد لحسن التعبير عنهما بالتثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sequence creates the earth, places mountains and blessings in it, then creates the heavens; spreading the earth is distinct and occurs later.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من هذه الآية أنه خلق الأرض وجعل فيها الرواسي وبارك فيها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics object that mountains, blessings, and provisions require an already spread earth, which seems to place the spread before heaven.
rows.anchor: وقد أورد على هذا أن جعل الرواسي فيها والبركة. وتقدير الأقوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further objection says the command to come signifies creation, so addressing an already created earth as if to create it is impossible.
rows.anchor: فلو سبق إيجاد الأرض على إيجاد السماء لاقتضى إيجاد الموجود بأمره

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says heaven was created before earth and treats the sequence marker as if an omitted “had been” were understood.
rows.anchor: ونقل الواحدي في البسيط عن مقاتل أنه قال: خلق الله السماء قبل الأرض،

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects combining ثم’s sequence with a past “had been,” since that would make the wording contradictory.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: فقدر ثم كان قد استوى جمع بين ضدين،

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi nevertheless prefers heaven-first chronology by interpreting creation as divine decree or determination rather than immediate bringing into existence.
rows.anchor: والمختار عندي أن يقال: خلق السماء مقدم على خلق الأرض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the rebuke concerns the one who produced all these things, not their chronology; ثم sequences the report rather than the creation events.
rows.anchor: أن الكفار وبخوا وقرعوا بكفرهم بمن صدرت عنه هذه الأشياء جميعها من غير ترتيب زماني،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse uses ثم because heaven’s creation is the more wondrous sign, much like report-ordering in other verses.
rows.anchor: ولما كان خلق السماء أبدع في القدرة من خلق الأرض، ألف الأخبار فيه بثم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to heaven and earth depicts the realization of God’s previously described creative will, as speech can illustrate praise already given.
rows.anchor: فهذا تصوير لما أثنيت به وتفسير له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counted days describe the duration in human terms and do not establish a temporal order among the acts of creation.
rows.anchor: وما جاء من ذلك مقصورا على يومين أو أربعة أو ستة إنما المعنى في مقدار ذلك عندكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He fashioned them as seven heavens” may parse سبع as a circumstantial accusative, a second object, or a specification of an ambiguous pronoun.
rows.anchor: فقضاهن سبع سماوات: أي صنعهن وأوجدهن،

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say God revealed to heaven’s angelic inhabitants and to heaven itself whatever sustains and orders it.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة: وأوحى إلى سكانها وعمرتها من الملائكة وإليها هي في نفسها

rows.speaker: السدي وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and Qatada include matters outside heaven that are associated with it, such as hailstones.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي وقتادة: ومن الأمور التي هي بغيرها مثل ما فيها من جبال البرد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari takes its “command” to include what God arranged there, such as angels and luminous bodies.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أمرها ما أمر به فيها ودبره من خلق الملائكة والنيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “As protection” most simply means that God guarded heaven from eavesdropping devils with shooting stars; an additional-purpose parse is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وحفظا: أي وحفظناها حفظا من المسترقة بالثواقب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If they turn away” shifts from direct address to third person because the audience has been given evidence that should have led them to believe.
rows.anchor: فإن أعرضوا: التفات خرج من ضمير الخطاب في قوله: قل أإنكم لتكفرون

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains the threatened thunderbolt as punishment like that of ‘Ad and Thamud.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: عذابا مثل عذاب عاد وثمود.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari describes the punishment as severe in impact, like a thunderbolt.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: عذابا شديد الوقع، كأنه صاعقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use صاعقة; Ibn al-Zubayr, al-Sulami, al-Nakha‘i, and Ibn Muhaysin read the form without an alif and with a still ‘ayn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: صاعقة مثل صاعقة، وابن الزبير، والسلمي، والنخعي، وابن محيصن:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word’s morphology is compared to other verbs in which the active form is followed by a passive form; “when” is governed by the word for thunderbolt because it means punishment.
rows.anchor: والصعقة: المرة، يقال: صعقته الصاعقة فصعق،
